subject: Emotions
title: Emotional Granularity
description: A short lesson to help you apply Emotional Granularity.

hook.text: You feel 'bad.' But is it disappointment, frustration, resentment, or grief? The difference matters for what to do next.

buildup.text: Lisa Feldman Barrett found people differ vastly in emotional granularity—how finely they distinguish feelings.

discovery.text: High-granularity people use precise labels: 'irritated' vs 'enraged.' Low-granularity people just say 'upset.'

twist.text: Greater granularity predicts better emotion regulation. If you can name it precisely, you can address it precisely.

climax.text: Barrett argues emotions aren't hardwired. Your brain constructs them from learned concepts—vocabulary shapes experience.

punchline.text: Learning more emotion words literally changes what you feel.

quiz.question: What does high emotional granularity predict?
